### First Majestic Reports Positive Exploration Results at Jerritt Canyon and Provides Restart Progress Update


November 12, 2026


*Strong exploration drilling results support the potential for open-pit mining as part of the restart plan*


*Jerritt Canyon continues to advance toward a targeted restart in the second half of 2027*


Vancouver, BC, Canada – First Majestic Silver Corp. (NYSE:AG) (TSX:AG) (FSE:FMV) (the “Company” or “First Majestic”) is pleased to announce positive drill results from its ongoing 2026 exploration program at the Jerritt Canyon Gold Mine ("Jerritt Canyon" or "JCG") in Nevada, USA. Near-surface drilling has returned significant gold intercepts that further support a potential open-pit operation at the mine. The Company also provides an update on the broader Jerritt Canyon restart plan, which continues to advance toward a targeted restart in the second half of 2027.


Near-surface reverse circulation (“RC”) drilling at Saval has returned significant gold intercepts containing higher-grade intervals. Highlights include 48.8 metres (“m”) grading 4.24 g/t Au, including 19.8 m at 7.39 g/t Au, in hole SC-26-030, and 36.6 m grading 5.87 g/t Au, including 9.1 m at 19.67 g/t Au, in hole SC-26-023. The results support continued evaluation of Saval as a source of open-pit mill feed that could complement underground production at the planned restart. The total surface drilling program has completed 15,983 m across 146 holes, with assays pending for many of the holes, particularly in the northern part of the property. Two diamond drill rigs are also following up on positive 2025 results in the Smith underground mine. Surface and underground drilling will continue through the end of 2026 and will continue into 2027.


*“At Jerritt Canyon, we are increasingly encouraged by Saval, where the existing open-pit permit, shallow mineralization and recent drill results highlight the potential for a meaningful source of open-pit mill feed alongside the underground operation.”* said Keith Neumeyer, CEO of First Majestic. *“We continue to make strong progress towards restarting Jerritt Canyon, with underground development advancing and critical upgrades to the processing plant and site infrastructure underway. Together, these initiatives continue to strengthen the opportunity for a successful restart of Jerritt Canyon”.*


**2026 EXPLORATION PROGRAM**


First Majestic continues an extensive surface RC drilling campaign to test near-surface gold mineralization and evaluate potential open-pit mining opportunities as part of the Jerritt Canyon restart studies. The historic Saval open-pit area is a key target within the program and is located northwest of the SSX and Smith underground mines.


The 2026 surface drilling program began at Saval, where 8,753 m were completed across 85 holes. In addition, targets in the northern part of the property have been advanced, where a further 7,230 m were completed across 61 holes. In total, the program has completed 15,983 m across 146 holes. The drilling is intended to improve geological confidence and to evaluate whether Mineral Resources at Jerritt Canyon can be expanded or upgraded in class. Assays remain pending for a substantial number of holes, particularly from the northern targets drilled later in the program.


Upon completion of drilling the targets in the northern part of the property, one rig was redeployed to evaluate gold mineralization at the Mahala and Javelin target areas surrounding the SSX and Smith underground mines, to follow up on the encouraging results returned in 2025. The second rig was reassigned to hydrogeological drilling to support key technical investigations for the restart. In parallel, two diamond drill rigs continued drilling within priority areas of the Smith underground mine, where preparations for the planned restart are advancing.

**SAVAL OPEN-PIT TARGET AREA**


Saval is a key target area in the Company’s evaluation of potential open-pit mill feed sources for the Jerritt Canyon restart. The area is already permitted for open-pit mining, which could allow future mining to advance without the permitting timelines commonly associated with developing a new open pit. Gold mineralization occurs in broad, near-surface, predominantly sub-horizontal zones that could support low strip ratios. Saval was historically mined at significantly higher cut-off grades, leaving lower-grade mineralization that was uneconomic at that time but may have value at current gold prices.


The 2026 drilling program was designed to better define the extent and continuity of mineralization remaining around the historical Saval pits, including areas where backfill obscures the limits of former mining. The program targeted mineralization remaining in the host bedrock to improve geological confidence and support potential additions and class upgrades to Mineral Resources. Follow-up work is planned in areas where the boundary between historical backfill and bedrock remains uncertain.


Drilling results include significant gold intercepts from both the northern and southeastern portions of Saval. Figure 2 below shows the drilling layout, selected significant intercepts and the locations of cross-sections A–A′ and B–B′.


Figure 2: Saval Historical Open Pit to SSX Underground Corridor Showing Cross-Sections A–A′ and B–B′. Plan View


**Northern Saval Area**


In the northern portion of Saval, drilling intersected continuous, near-surface gold mineralization, as shown along section A–A′, and provided additional information to support the evaluation of Mineral Resource classification upgrades.


Highlighted results include 48.8 m grading 4.24 g/t Au, including 19.8 m at 7.39 g/t Au, in hole SC-26-030, and 36.6 m grading 5.87 g/t Au, including 9.1 m at 19.67 g/t Au, in hole SC-26-023. These broad intercepts contain significant higher-grade intervals and further support the assessment of North Saval as a potential source of open-pit mill feed. Figure 3 plots the drilling results and geological interpretation along section A–A′.


Figure 3: Northern Saval Cross-Section A–A′. Section Location Shown in Figure 2; Section Thickness ±27.5 m


**Southeast Saval Area**


In the southeast portion of Saval, drilling along section B–B′ tested shallow gold mineralization identified by historical drilling and helped define the boundary between backfill in the open pits and mineralized bedrock.


Drilling returned multiple significant near-surface gold intercepts. The broad, shallow mineralized intervals support continued evaluation of Southeast Saval as a potential open-pit Resource. Additional work is required where RC drilling did not clearly identify the boundary between backfill and bedrock. Figure 4 shows the drilling results and geological interpretation along section B–B’.


Figure 4: Southeast Saval Cross-Section B–B′. Section Location Shown in Figure 2; Section Thickness ±27.5 m

**JERRITT CANYON GOLD MINE RESTART UPDATE**


Jerritt Canyon continues to advance toward a targeted restart of operations in the second half of 2027. Senior leadership and key technical roles have been filled, while underground development and rehabilitation are advancing toward the initial planned mining areas. Technical, engineering and operational readiness activities are also progressing. Work remains focused on defining the optimal pathway to sustained, long-term production, with recent drilling results further supporting the potential for combined underground and open-pit operations.


The Company continues to advance with the initial restart plan announced on April 2, 2026, and has brought forward investments from 2027 into 2026. Some of these investments include the foundation work for a vertical roller mill ("VRM") and long-lead mining and processing equipment.


The Company’s decision to replace the existing crushing, grinding and drying circuit at Jerritt Canyon with a VRM is a key component of the restart plan. The VRM will prepare ore from the underground and potential open-pit operations for processing through the existing roasting facility. The new circuit is expected to provide a more reliable and efficient feed to the plant, increase throughput, reduce operating costs and improve utilization of Jerritt Canyon’s existing roasting capacity.


The Company also completed the acquisition of an adjacent property, totaling 2,971 Acres (1,202 Hectares). The additional land is expected to support mine dewatering requirements and provide potential employee accommodation very close to site. This purchase includes several liveable buildings allowing the staff at Jerritt Canyon to live on site saving people travel time to and from the mine each day. The purchase of this strategic land package may also provide conservation offsets to support future permitting requirements beyond the current mine plan.


The ongoing technical studies and exploration programs will inform the restart plan, with findings to be summarized in an updated technical report (the “Report”) that will be prepared in accordance with National Instrument 43-101 *Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects* (“NI 43-101”), which the Company expects to issue at the end of Q1 2027. The Report will incorporate the latest available exploration, engineering and mine planning information. Mine planning and engineering will continue beyond the issuance of the Report as additional drilling results and technical information are incorporated into the restart plan.


**QUALITY ASSURANCE AND QUALITY CONTROL**


First Majestic’s drilling programs at Jerritt Canyon follow established quality assurance and quality control (“QA/QC”) protocols, including the insertion of standards, blanks and duplicates into the sample stream. All RC drill-hole samples were placed in bags labelled with the hole ID, sample ID and sample interval, and were submitted to Bureau Veritas Minerals Laboratories (“BV”), an ISO/IEC 17025:2017-accredited laboratory.


At BV, samples are dried, crushed to 70% passing 2 mm and pulverized to 85% passing 75 μm. Gold is analyzed by lead-collection fire assay with an atomic absorption spectrometry finish (FA430). Samples returning gold grades above 10 g/t are reanalyzed using a 30 g lead-collection fire assay with a gravimetric finish (FA530).

**ABOUT FIRST MAJESTIC**


First Majestic is a publicly traded mining company focused on silver and gold production in Mexico and the United States. The Company presently owns and operates four producing underground mines in Mexico: the Los Gatos Silver Mine (the Company holds a 70% interest in the Los Gatos Joint Venture that owns and operates the mine), the Santa Elena Silver/Gold Mine, the San Dimas Silver/Gold Mine, and the La Encantada Silver Mine, as well as a portfolio of development and exploration assets, including the Jerritt Canyon Gold Mine located in northeastern Nevada, U.S.A, which the Company is currently in the process of re-starting.
